page.layout: Two engraved coin medallions centred at the top, with their legends around the rims. Below them, one column of running text in two paragraphs, full width. The running head is at the top, with the page number at the left.

main_text.p: ZOE, ab exilio & monasterio assentiente universa plebe (uti dictum à me est) reuocata, & Michaële Calaphate exoculato, imperij faces suscipit Constantinopolitani, unà cum sorore Theodora. anno mundi eodem quo Michaël Calaphates quatuor mensesimperauit: itaque flagitia Imperatorum effecere ut muliebre æquius videretur imperium. At verò, cùm sit varium, ac mutabile semper Fœmina, ut inquit poëta, Zoë sexagenaria, ardens tamen adhuc libidine, Constantinum Monomachum ab exilio reuocat, sibíque eum maritû adiungit: curátque ut sceptrû imperij illi tradatur, cùm fœminarum vix treis mēses durasset imperiû. Vide Egna.lib.2.Cosmog.Munst.lib.4.

CONSTANTINUS Monomachus, imperatorij quidem & ipse stemmatis, quem sibi in virum asciuit Zoë, Constantinopoli imperat anno mundi 5005. à Christo nato 1043. Hic ignauus, & luxu totus diffluens, concubinam, egregia alioqui forma, iustæ uxoris loco habuit, quam efflictim deperiit. Sustinuit tamen duo grauissima bella ciuilia, alterum à Maniace Georgio, alterum à Leone Tornicio, illata: & multa externa. Turcarum arma tunc primù per Asiam latius sunt euagata: victi tamen Roxolani, & Patzinacæ, Scythicum genus hominum. Zoë uxore septuagenaria fato mox functa, & ipse tandem podagricus, & pleuritide correptus obiit, anno imperij fere 13. Vide ut supra.

page.notes: The two medallions are engravings, not printed text. Left medallion: a double portrait of two crowned women, with the legend "ZOE ET THEODORA". Right medallion: a bearded, crowned man in profile, with the legend "CONSTANT. MONOMACH.". Part of the left medallion's legend is hard to read in the scan. Printed "mensesimperauit" has no space, as in the original. The date "5005" is set in old-style figures, read as 5005. The running head is read as "PROMPTV. ICONVM" and normalised to u/v spelling as "PROMPTU. ICONUM".
